Answer: C
Reason: Comparing Figure 1 and Figure 2 reveals that the initial dense consolidation in the left lung has significantly resolved, while new patchy opacities have appeared in the right upper lung. This radiographic pattern of resolving infiltrates in one location accompanied by new infiltrates in another is characteristic of migratory pulmonary opacities, a hallmark finding of Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia (COP).
